summary:
Sergipe's own constitutional layer is older than most in Brazil: in 1989 the state, alongside Mato Grosso do Sul, was among the first to write a ban on sexual-orientation discrimination into its constitution. On 17 December 2025 Constitutional Amendment No. 59, proposed by state deputy Linda Brasil (PSOL), amended article 3(II) of the State Constitution to guarantee protection against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, with violators subject to punishment by law, effective on promulgation. Sergipe is the first Brazilian state to write gender-identity protection into its constitution.

The state judiciary has its own marriage provision. On 5 July 2012 the State Judiciary Power issued Provimento nº 06/2012, which regulated same-sex marriage throughout Sergipe. Since 2025 the state has allowed individuals to change their gender marker on documents to non-binary.

Court facilities in the state capital are explicitly gender-neutral. From 28 August 2025 the Court of Justice of Sergipe provides operating gender-neutral bathrooms on the ground, first and eighth floors of the Palácio da Justiça in Aracaju, usable by any person regardless of gender identity. The same measure directs that in all Sergipe judiciary units male and female bathrooms be used respecting each person's gender identity, under human-rights and non-discrimination principles, and requires that all new constructions and renovations be planned with gender-equity demands.

Institutional access has widened at the state's federal university. On 17 November 2025 the Federal University of Sergipe approved affirmative-action quotas for trans people in undergraduate courses.

A counter-current sits in the state legislature. On 1 December 2020 state deputy Rodrigo Valadares (UNIÃO) tabled a bill to prohibit the use and teaching of gender-neutral language in Sergipe's public and private schools and in state public offices, requiring traditional Portuguese in schools, official notices and public offices.
tangentialFactors:
Sergipe's 2025 amendment places it ahead of the other states on constitutional gender-identity protection; its 1989 sexual-orientation clause was shared at the time only with Mato Grosso do Sul. Both are state-level constitutional texts rather than general public-accommodation rules.

The measures with the most concrete physical effect are institutional in scope. The gender-neutral bathrooms and the directive on use of male and female facilities apply to judiciary units, and the trans quota applies to the Federal University of Sergipe; neither governs private commercial premises, hospitality or transport in the state.
localsOnly:
Trans residents hold a state-constitutional anti-discrimination guarantee: article 3(II) of the State Constitution, as amended on 17 December 2025, covers sexual orientation and gender identity and makes violators subject to punishment by law. The 1989 sexual-orientation clause it builds on was one of the first in Brazil.

State documents allow a non-binary gender marker in Sergipe as of 2025, and the state judiciary's 2012 provision regulates marriage for same-sex couples throughout the state.

The Federal University of Sergipe reserves undergraduate places for trans students under quotas approved on 17 November 2025.

Court users in Aracaju have gender-neutral bathrooms at the Palácio da Justiça, and judiciary units statewide are directed to let people use male and female bathrooms according to their gender identity.

A 2020 bill by state deputy Rodrigo Valadares would bar gender-neutral language in Sergipe's schools and public offices, requiring traditional Portuguese in teaching, official notices and public administration.

The legislative status of the December 2020 bill on gender-neutral language is not recorded in the sources; whether it was enacted, rejected or remains pending is unresolved.

No region-specific enforcement data, violence statistics or police practice for Sergipe appears in the inventory. The state-level protections are recorded as law and institutional policy, not as documented enforcement outcomes.

The scope of the non-binary document marker in Sergipe, including which state documents and agencies offer it, is not detailed in the sources.
